newsitem.title: JAPAN: Two Osaka credit unions to merge.
newsitem.headline: Two Osaka credit unions to merge.

text.p: Two western Japan credit unions, Hanna Shinkin Bank and Fuji Shinkin Bank, will merge in an effort to ride out Japan's financial deregulation, their directors announced on Saturday.
Hanna Shinkin Bank, with deposits of 216.29 billion yen ($1.86 billion) and total lending of 175.43 billion yen ($1.51 billion), ranks 129th of the 414 shinkin banks in Japan.
Fuji has deposits of 22.18 billion yen ($191 million) and total lending of 15.60 billion yen ($134 million), and ranks close to the bottom of the list.
Shinkin banks, which operate in a similar fashion to credit unions, are made up of regional investors and focus on lending mostly to small-to-medium sized companies.

The merged bank, also called Hanna Shinkin Bank, will have deposits of 238.48 billion yen ($2.05 billion) and lending of 191.04 billion yen ($1.64 billion), with 26 branches scattered over Osaka. The merger is expected to be completed in October.
"With our size, we cannot grow or develop further without a merger," Fuji Shinkin's director Takao Inoue said.
Inoue said he had started thinking about merger options five years ago, when the burst of the economic bubble in Japan started hurting his business.
Hanna Shinkin's director Yasuhiro Ueda said, "The shinkin banks, deeply rooted to their own regions, will be the ones to survive amidst Japan's Big Bang."
Hanna Shinkin said its bad loans totalled 4.5 billion yen ($38.7 million) while Fuji Shinkin's stood at 121 million yen ($1.04 million).
Tomoe Shindo, Chairman of the Osaka Association for Shinkin Banks, said, "This should be taken as bright news when there are so many bad ones hanging above the financial world of Japan."
Asked whether there could be more mergers, he said, "I haven't seen any come to the surface yet, but if they are talks in the good direction, why not?"
There are 21 shinkin banks in Osaka.
